summary: P99 latency spikes and request timeouts in prod tied to continuous batching behavior
description: Issue summary: ShopNow reported increased p95/p99 generation latencies and intermittent request timeouts for their dedicated routes starting 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC. Customer reported elevated 5xx and client-visible timeouts for interactive endpoints. Impact: User-facing checkout suggestion flows slowed and timed out intermittently leading to elevated error rate and customer tickets. Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool (shopnow-dedicated-1), API route shopnow/v1/generate. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of short-chat requests (seq_len 32-128) at 120 req/s to customer route. 2) Observe p95/p99 latency in Redwood Console metrics and increase in gateway 504s. Observed behavior: p50 stable (~60ms), p95 jumps to 700-1200ms, p99 spikes to 2-6s and occasional 5xx/timeouts. Logs show long tail in serving-runtime request queue and periodic batching behavior where a small number of requests are held and then released as a single large batch. Expected behavior: Continuous batching should maintain bounded latency; p99 should not exceed 1s for these request sizes in dedicated pool. Initial mitigation: disabled continuous batching heuristic for shopnow route, which reduced p99 to ~400-600ms. Follow-ups needed: determine root cause in scheduler heuristics or kernel selection that causes occasional batch hold/flush and investigate interaction with quantized kernels for gpt-neoxt-20b-quant.
investigation: 03-01 10:00 UTC - Support: Received customer report and created ticket. Collected customer route, sample request traces, and recent console graphs.
03-01 11:15 UTC - SRE: Observed synchronized batch flush events every ~30-90s correlated with p99 spikes. CPU on the scheduler occasionally saturates at those times.

03-01 12:30 UTC - Eng (serving-runtime): Reproduced locally by running load-generator against dedicated pool; reproduced p99 spikes when continuous batching target window is met and KV cache warmup interacts with quantized execution path.

03-02 09:20 UTC - Hypothesis: Under certain interarrival patterns the continuous-batching controller delays small batches to hit an efficiency threshold; when combined with a slow kernel selection path for quantized models, requests get held leading to high tail latency.
03-02 14:05 UTC - Temporary mitigation: Disabled continuous batching policy (heuristic) for shopnow route via config toggle (config change id: cfg-2026-03-shopnow-01). Metrics improved immediately.
03-03 08:40 UTC - Observed that disabling batching reduced p99 but increased overall token cost by ~6% for the customer; customer accepted temporary tradeoff.

03-03 16:50 UTC - Next steps: instrument more detailed timing in batching controller, add metrics around kernel selection path, and test patch that short-circuits batching when quantized-kernel latency > threshold.
Related notes: See linked issues SUP-4821 and SUP-10642 for historical continuous-batching regressions and prior mitigations.

Root cause under investigation: interaction between continuous-batching controller thresholds and quantized-kernel selection causing delayed batch flushes.
